messages.content: generate a threlte component that loads a texture and shows it like a splash screen

1. Create the `SplashScreen` class with React's functional components syntax, which is more suitable for stateless components like this one. 2. Import the image you want to use as your splash screen from its location in your project directory using JavaScript's ES6 import statement. 3. Use CSS-in-JS techniques (such as styled-components or Emotion) to style the container element of the splash screen. You can set properties such as background color, width, height, etc., according to your needs. 4. Inside the return function, render an `` tag with the imported image source (`src`) attribute pointing to the imported image file. This will display the image on the page when the SplashScreen component mounts. 5. Optionally, add some animation effects to make the transition between the splash screen and the main content smoother. For example, you could fade out the splash screen after a certain amount of time has passed or when the user clicks anywhere on the screen. 6. Finally, export the `SplashScreen` component so other parts of your application can easily access it. 7. Include the `SplashScreen` component inside another parent component where you would normally show your app's initial content. Make sure to remove the `SplashScreen` once the desired conditions are met (e.g., loading data finished).
